agileload.about: AgileLoad is an enterprise-class load, stress, and performance testing tool by Quotium Technologies (AgileLoad SAS, a subsidiary of Quotium) that simulates concurrent user traffic for web, mobile, and API applications from on-premises or cloud environments, with real-time monitoring, automatic anomaly detection/diagnostics, and custom report generation. aiperf.about: AIPerf is a comprehensive open-source benchmarking tool from NVIDIA (ai-dynamo project) that measures the performance of generative AI models served by inference solutions. It is the designated successor to GenAI-Perf, a ground-up multiprocess rewrite that generates load against inference endpoints (OpenAI-compatible APIs, NIM, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, etc.) and reports detailed metrics such as TTFT, ITL, request latency, and output token throughput, with CLI display and extensive benchmark reports.
features: Scalable multiprocess architecture with 10 services communicating via ZMQ
3 UI modes: dashboard (real-time TUI), simple (progress bars), none (headless)
Benchmarking modes: concurrency, request-rate, request-rate with max concurrency, trace replay
Extensible plugin system for endpoints, datasets, transports, and metrics
Public dataset support (ShareGPT, AIMO, MMStar, MMVU, VisionArena, LLaVA-OneVision, SpecBench, ASR datasets, etc.) and custom/inline datasets
Load control: constant/Poisson/gamma arrival patterns, gradual ramping, warmup phase, request cancellation, multi-URL load balancing
Trace replay from production sources (Bailian, Baseten, BurstGPT, SageMaker, Weka, TraceLab, H CUA Perf traces)
15+ supported endpoint types including OpenAI chat/completions/embeddings/audio/images, NIM embeddings/rankings, Anthropic Messages API, audio_transcription

ali.about: ali is an open-source HTTP load testing tool written in Go that generates HTTP load against a target URL and plots the results in real-time in an embedded terminal-based UI, inspired by vegeta and jplot. It supports configurable request rate, duration, workers, headers, bodies, TLS options, HTTP/2, and exporting results for downstream processing.
features: Real-time terminal UI plotting latency, percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), and other metrics during load tests
Configurable request rate, duration, workers, connections, timeout, and query range
Custom HTTP methods, headers, request bodies (inline or from file)
TLS support (CA cert, client cert/key, insecure mode) and HTTP/2 with options to disable
Mouse support and interactive chart zooming (latency, percentiles, bytes, histogram charts)
Export load test results to a directory for downstream processing (--export-to)
Attack progress visualization for long tests
Custom DNS resolvers, local address binding, keep-alive control

apache-jmeter.about: Apache JMeter is open source, 100% pure Java software designed to load test functional behavior and measure performance. Originally designed for testing Web Applications, it has expanded to test many protocol types (HTTP/HTTPS, SOAP/REST, FTP, JDBC databases, LDAP, JMS, SMTP/POP3/IMAP, TCP, shell commands, Java objects). features: Load and performance testing of many protocol types: Web HTTP/HTTPS, SOAP/REST webservices, FTP, JDBC databases, LDAP, JMS, Mail (SMTP(S), POP3(S), IMAP(S)), native commands/shell scripts, TCP, Java objects
Full-featured Test IDE with test plan recording (from browsers or native applications), building, and debugging
CLI/headless (non-GUI) mode for load testing from any Java-compatible OS (Linux, Windows, macOS)
Dynamic HTML dashboard report, ready to present
Live reporting into 3rd-party databases like InfluxDB or Graphite
Easy correlation via data extraction from HTML, JSON, XML, or any textual response format
Complete portability and 100% Java purity
Multi-threading framework for concurrent sampling by many threads and separate thread groups

apachebench.about: ApacheBench (ab) is a single-threaded, command-line HTTP server benchmarking tool written in C that ships with the Apache HTTP Server. It opens multiple concurrent connections to a URL, sends a specified number of HTTP requests, and reports throughput metrics such as requests per second, time per request, transfer rate, and latency percentiles. It can test any HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1 web server, not just Apache.
features: HTTP benchmarking with configurable request count (-n) and concurrency level (-c)
HTTP KeepAlive support (-k)
Custom HTTP methods (-m) and custom headers (-H)
POST and PUT data support with content-type specification (-p, -u, -T)
SSL/TLS support including protocol selection (-f) and cipher suite specification (-Z), TLSv1.3 support when the SSL library supports it, and OpenSSL 4.0 support
Client certificate authentication for SSL (-E, available in 2.4.36 and later)
Basic authentication for server and proxy (-A, -P)
Proxy server support (-X)

apex-hammer.about: Apex Hammer is Salesforce's internal automated regression-testing process run before each major platform release. Salesforce runs an org's Apex unit tests twice — once in the current production version and once in the release-candidate version — and compares the results to detect behavior changes in custom code, triaging and fixing regressions before the release is deployed. Orgs are selected selectively (not all orgs run every cycle), and admins can view execution status/results in Setup under Apex Hammer Test Results.
features: Automated execution of an org's Apex unit tests twice per major release cycle (current version vs. release candidate)
Side-by-side comparison of test results to identify regressions in custom code before release deployment
Selective org execution — the process runs only on a subset of orgs per release cycle
Issue triaging by priority and platform impact, with Salesforce engineering fixing issues before rollout
Execution status visibility in Setup (Apex Hammer Test Results), showing the org's latest historical run if no tests ran for the current release
Runs in Salesforce's secure data centers without exposing org data or debug logs
apex-hammer.pricing: Included as part of the Salesforce platform service; operated by Salesforce and not sold or licensed separately.

apib.about: apib (API Bench) is a simple, fast, open-source HTTP and API benchmarking/performance-testing tool by Google Apigee. It is a modernized ApacheBench-like CLI utility for running time-scheduled load tests against HTTP/1.1 API servers, with support for concurrent connections, keep-alives, chunked encoding, POST/PUT of large objects, OAuth 1.0 signatures, CSV output for automation, and local/remote CPU and memory monitoring via the companion apibmon program. It builds on most Linux platforms, Mac OS X, and FreeBSD, and can be installed via Homebrew. The repository is archived (last release 1.2.1, published as a release candidate in 2020).
features: HTTP/1.1-only benchmarking with configurable keep-alive and chunked encoding
Time-scheduled load tests with configurable concurrent connections (e.g., apib -c 100 -d 60 URL)
Multiple I/O threads (one per CPU core) with non-blocking I/O for high concurrency
Support for POST and PUT of large request bodies, HTTP verbs, request headers, and HTTP Basic authentication
Built-in OAuth 1.0 signature support
Output results to screen or CSV file for automated testing
Local and remote CPU/memory monitoring via apibmon (Linux-like systems, /proc-based)
Latency calculations, error counts, socket counts, and throughput reporting during and after runs
apib.pricing: Free and open source under the Apache License 2.0; no commercial pricing (repository is archived; available via Homebrew and source build).

azure-load-testing.about: Azure Load Testing is a fully managed, cloud-scale load-testing service by Microsoft (now part of Azure App Testing, introduced Aug 7, 2025) that generates high-scale load to simulate traffic for applications hosted anywhere (Azure, on-premises, or other clouds). It supports quick URL-based tests and script-based tests using Apache JMeter or Locust, up to 400 engine instances per run simulating up to 100,000 virtual users, with dashboards showing client-side and server-side (Azure Monitor/Application Insights) metrics, CI/CD integration, multi-region load tests, private endpoint testing, and AI-powered test authoring and insights.

Script-based tests using Apache JMeter (all JMeter protocols: HTTP/HTTPS, TCP, JDBC, LDAP, FTP) and Locust
High-scale load: up to 400 engine instances per test run, up to 100,000 virtual users
Multi-region load tests simulating traffic from multiple regions
Testing of public and private endpoints (VNet/on-premises apps)

Test run history with visual comparison of multiple runs and baseline comparison to detect regressions
CI/CD pipeline integration with test fail criteria and auto-stop on error conditions

VUH = (# virtual users × duration in minutes) / 60, measured every 10 seconds with fractional billing.
aiFeatures: AI-powered actionable insights: AI analyzes test run data/logs to detect issues (latency spikes, throughput drops, bottlenecks), identify root causes of failed runs, and provide recommended next steps
Baseline comparison insights using AI to show what degraded/improved versus a defined baseline and root-cause analysis of performance degradation
AI-generated test plan recommendations from uploaded browser recording files (GenerateTestPlanRecommendations API)

JMeter JMX file upload and execution via web dashboard
Distributed load generation across multiple AWS regions using your own AWS account and pre-configured AMI

baton.about: Baton is an open-source HTTP/HTTPS load testing tool written in Go, created by American Express. It is a CLI tool that supports GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE requests, with configurable concurrency, request counts or test duration, request bodies, custom headers, and CSV-based request files. The repository is archived (no longer actively maintained) and licensed under Apache License 2.0.
features: HTTP load testing with GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE requests
Configurable number of concurrent requests (workers)
Run by fixed number of requests or by test duration in seconds
Request body via inline string (-b) or file (-f)
CSV request file support (RFC-4180) with per-request method, URL, body, and headers
TLS/SSL certificate validation option (-i to ignore)
Optional wait period before starting the test (-w)
Suppressed output mode (-o)

bees-with-machine-guns.about: Bees with Machine Guns is an open-source Python utility for arming (creating) many bees (micro EC2 instances) to attack (load test) targets (web applications). It orchestrates AWS EC2 instances via boto/paramiko to generate distributed HTTP load against a target URL, with commands to up, attack, down, and report on the load-testing instances.

Commands: up (start load-testing servers), attack (send concurrent HTTP requests to a target URL), down (shutdown instances), report (status of load-testing servers)
Configurable attack parameters: number of connections, concurrent connections, HTTP headers, cookies, POST files, MIME types, SSL/TLS ciphers, keep-alive, basic auth
CSV output of result distribution across completed bees
Hurl integration for HTTP load testing with multithreading, parallelism, SSL, and rate limiting options
Multi-regional testing: launch bees from multiple AWS regions simultaneously with a single command
Per-region summarized attack output with optional long output details
Python 2.6–3.6 support with boto and paramiko dependencies

benchbase.about: BenchBase (formerly OLTPBench) is an open-source, multi-DBMS SQL benchmarking framework via JDBC developed by the Carnegie Mellon Database Group. It is a multi-threaded load generator that produces variable-rate, variable-mixture workloads against any JDBC-enabled relational database (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, CockroachDB, Spanner, Oracle, SQL Server), with 18+ built-in benchmarks (TPC-C, TPC-H, YCSB, SEATS, Twitter, AuctionMark, CH-benCHmark, SmallBank, TATP, etc.) and per-transaction latency/throughput data collection.
features: Multi-threaded load generation with precise request rate control (variable over time)
Precise transactional mixture control (change % of each transaction type over time)
Access distribution control (emulate hot-spots, temporal skew; uniform/binomial/zipfian/scrambled distributions in templated queries)
Trace-based execution for real data

18+ built-in benchmarks: TPC-C, TPC-H, YCSB, SEATS, Twitter, AuctionMark, CH-benCHmark, SmallBank, TATP, SIBench, Epinions, Wikipedia, Voter, OT-Metrics, Resource Stresser, NoOp, templated custom benchmarks
Supports major relational DBMSs and DBaaS via JDBC (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, CockroachDB, Spanner, Oracle, SQL Server, DB2, HSQLDB, Amazon RDS)
Statistics collection with microsecond latency/throughput precision and OS resource utilization
Throughput and advanced monitoring modes (query plans, cache hits, system metrics for SQLServer/Postgres)

benchmarkdotnet.about: BenchmarkDotNet is a powerful .NET benchmarking library that helps you transform methods into benchmarks, track their performance, and share reproducible measurement experiments. It uses the Perfolizer and PragmaStat statistical engines for reliable, precise results, protects against common benchmarking pitfalls, and presents results in user-friendly summary tables. It is adopted by 27,400+ GitHub projects including the .NET Runtime, .NET Compiler, and .NET Performance teams. Supported runtimes: .NET 5+, .NET Framework 4.6.1+, .NET Core 2.0+, Mono, NativeAOT; languages: C#, F#, Visual Basic; OS: Windows, Linux, macOS; architectures: x86, x64, ARM, ARM64, Wasm, LoongArch64.
features: Declarative attribute-based and fluent API benchmark design with [Params], [Benchmark(Baseline=true)], and jobs for multi-runtime comparison
Automatic pilot runs, warmup iterations, overhead measurement, and statistical parameter selection (Perfolizer/PragmaStat)
Diagnosers: MemoryDiagnoser (GC allocations, managed/native memory traffic), DisassemblyDiagnoser (code size and disassembly listings), ThreadingDiagnoser, dotMemory and dotTrace profiler integration
Exporters for multiple formats: CSV, JSON, XML, HTML, Markdown, plots (RPlotExporter), and OpenMetrics/Prometheus-compatible metrics export (v0.15.8)
Roslyn analyzers for benchmark code validation (multi-target, BDN1503 argument/params diagnostics)
Multi-runtime support: .NET 5+, .NET Framework 4.6.1+, Mono, NativeAOT, WebAssembly (Mono and CoreCLR toolchains)
In-process toolchains including InProcessNoEmitToolchain (reflection-based) and IL-emitting async support for async/await and async enumerables
Command-line interface with options like --exporters, --list json, custom exporters, and job categories

Performance/load testing for web, mobile, APIs, and microservices

bombardier.about: Bombardier is a fast, cross-platform HTTP(S) benchmarking and load-testing CLI tool written in Go. It uses the fasthttp library by default for high performance and can optionally use Go's net/http client (via --http1/--http2 flags) for HTTP/2.x testing or more RFC-compliant behavior. It supports timed and request-count-limited test modes, concurrent connections, rate limiting, custom headers/bodies, TLS options, latency statistics, and user-defined output templates.
features: Cross-platform CLI (Windows, macOS, Linux, BSD) written in Go
HTTP/HTTPS benchmarking with fasthttp client by default
Optional net/http client with forced HTTP/1.x or enabled HTTP/2.0 (--http1/--http2)
Configurable concurrent connections, request count, duration, and rate limit (requests/sec)
Custom HTTP method, request body (inline or from file), chunked streaming, and repeatable custom headers
TLS support: client certificate/key and --insecure option
Latency statistics with percentiles (50/75/90/99) and HTTP status code breakdown
Output formats: plain-text and JSON, plus user-defined Go text/template output templates

browserstack-load-testing.about: BrowserStack Load Testing is a cloud-based, AI-powered load testing platform that runs real browser and API traffic in the same test. It lets teams simulate up to 1 million API virtual users and 1,000 browser virtual users per test across multiple regions on fully managed cloud infrastructure, combining browser load testing (Playwright, Selenium, WebdriverIO, Nightwatch), API load testing (JMeter, k6, Gatling, Locust), and hybrid scenarios, with unified frontend (Core Web Vitals), backend, and APM metrics on one dashboard. Low-code recorder to create load tests without scripting
Unified dashboard correlating Core Web Vitals, server response times, throughput, error rates, and APM data (Datadog, New Relic integrations)
Multi-region load zones across North America, Europe, and Asia on fully managed cloud infrastructure
CI/CD integration with Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab with performance regression thresholds/SLAs
Shareable trend, failure, and bottleneck reports
MCP server to create, run, monitor, and analyze load tests from AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT)

Real-browser load testing (no simulation) plus API/HTTP-level tests

Rich reporting suite and Report Studio for custom reports; scalability benchmarking
CI/CD-ready workflow with YAML (browserup.load.yaml) scenario config: profiles, ramp stages, think time, databanks (CSV), proxy filtering options

Counter column workloads (counter_write, counter_read)

Latency sampling and statistics reporting (-sample, -reporting)
HTML graph generation of recorded metrics with revisions for comparing multiple runs (-graph)

criterion-rs.about: Criterion.rs is a statistics-driven micro-benchmarking library for Rust (a Rust port of Haskell's Criterion). curl-loader.about: curl-loader is an open-source, C-written load/performance testing tool (also known as 'omes-nik' and 'davilka') that simulates application load and behavior of thousands to tens of thousands of HTTP/HTTPS and FTP/FTPS clients, each with its own source IP address. It uses real client protocol stacks — libcurl for HTTP/FTP and OpenSSL for TLS/SSL — and is positioned as an open-source alternative to Spirent Avalanche and IXIA IxLoad. It runs on Linux and is licensed under GPLv2.
features: 2,500–100,000+ simultaneous virtual loading clients from a single process, each with its own (or shared) source IP address
Rampup of virtual client count in automatic or manual mode
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and URIs

Playback file support (-f) for replaying recorded requests

High concurrency using Go goroutines (up to 65535 clients/ports)
HTTP GET and POST requests (POST with data file via -d)
Keep-alive connection option (-k)
Configurable number of concurrent clients (-c) and test duration (-t)
Reports request hits, successful requests, failed requests, requests/sec rate, and read/write throughput

Cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux)

features: C++ microbenchmarking with automatic iteration count selection and warm-up
Repeated runs with mean, median, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation statistics
Parameterized benchmarks and fixtures (GoogleTest-like API)
Asymptotic (Big O) complexity analysis
User counters and hardware performance counters (libpfm)
Console, JSON, and CSV output formats
Manual timing (UseManualTime/SetIterationTime) and pause/resume timing (ScopedPauseTiming)
Multithreaded benchmarks with barrier synchronization

goose.about: Goose is an open-source load testing framework written in Rust, inspired by Locust, developed by Tag1 Consulting. Load tests are small Rust programs built with Cargo that simulate realistic user behavior (logins, form fills, navigation) across scenarios and transactions, with metrics, reports, and a live dashboard.
features: Rust-based, fast and scalable load testing (async users on Tokio multi-threaded runtime)
Scenarios and transactions with weighting, sequencing, and scheduling (round-robin, serial, random)
Realistic user behavior simulation (logins, forms, navigation) via Reqwest HTTP client with cookies
Live web dashboard streaming RPS, users, and latency charts over SSE with optional authenticated Start/Stop/control
MCP Controller exposing all Controller commands as Model Context Protocol tools for AI agents
Reports in HTML, Markdown, PDF, and JSON with microsecond-precision timing and baseline comparison
Thresholds that can fail a CI run when metrics degrade; runs as a single binary in CI or containers
Distributed load testing via Gaggles (manager/worker)
goose.pricing: Free and open source, Apache License 2.0; no pricing tiers documented.

goreplay.about: GoReplay is an open-source tool (written in Go) that captures live HTTP traffic from production and replays it into an isolated test environment for shadow testing, load testing, debugging, and reproducing production bugs. It works via raw socket packet capture (libpcap) without sitting in the application path, and supports request filtering, rewriting, and middleware. It runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
features: HTTP traffic capture via raw socket sniffing (libpcap) and replay to test endpoints
Request filtering, rewriting, and Go middleware plugins
File-based capture and replay (local files, gzip, pcap) for deterministic load testing
Controlled replay speed (speed up/slow down) and replay to multiple endpoints simultaneously
Shadow testing of new builds against production traffic
Load testing with real production traffic mix and latency/error metrics
Debugging and reproduction: inspect captured requests, replay filtered samples, compare responses
Outputs to HTTP endpoints, local files, TCP streams, Kafka, and Elasticsearch

grafana-cloud-k6.about: Grafana Cloud k6 is Grafana Labs' fully managed, cloud-based performance and load testing platform built on the open-source k6 engine. It lets cross-functional teams (developers, QA, SDETs, SREs) test at scale, prevent system failures, and deliver fast, reliable applications — with distributed cloud load tests from 20+ geographic load zones, up to 1 million concurrent virtual users or 5 million requests/second, Private Load Zones for internal systems, and results visualized in Grafana Cloud dashboards.
features: Distributed cloud load testing from 20+ geographic load zones, up to 1 million concurrent virtual users or 5 million requests/second
Private Load Zones for securely testing internal services and additional regions
k6 Studio: visual test creation, recording of user flows into test scripts, and visual script editing/debugging
Playwright-inspired k6 browser API for frontend performance testing with Web Vitals reports, interaction timelines, and screenshots
Protocol-level (HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, GraphQL) and browser-level testing combined
Scheduling and automation from web app, CLI, and CI pipelines with SLOs as pass/fail criteria
Cloud Insights to automatically surface performance-related problems in test results
k6 visualizations integrated into existing Grafana Cloud dashboards

It lets engineering teams (developers, QA, SDETs, SREs) run load/performance tests (spike, stress, soak), browser-based performance tests via a Playwright-inspired browser API, synthetic monitoring, CI/CD-automated performance testing, chaos/resilience testing, and infrastructure testing via extensions. features: Load and performance testing (spike, stress, soak) with minimal resource consumption
Browser performance testing via Playwright-inspired k6 browser API with Web Vitals metrics, interaction timelines, and screenshots
Performance and synthetic monitoring (scheduled low-load tests, Grafana Cloud Synthetic Monitoring integration)
CI/CD and automation integration for automated performance testing
Chaos and resilience testing (traffic simulation, xk6-disruptor fault injection in Kubernetes)
Extensible via k6 extensions for new protocols and clients
JavaScript scripting with checks, thresholds, and configuration as code

grafana-k6-browser.about: k6 browser is the browser module of k6, Grafana Labs' open-source load testing tool. It brings browser automation and end-to-end web testing to k6, adding Playwright-inspired browser-level APIs (via Chrome DevTools Protocol) to interact with Chromium-based browsers and collect frontend performance metrics (e.g., Web Vitals, page load time) as part of k6 tests, alongside protocol-level load testing.
features: Playwright-inspired browser automation APIs (Page, BrowserContext, Locator, ElementHandle, Keyboard, Mouse, Touchscreen) for clicking, typing, and navigation
End-to-end web testing with frontend performance metrics and Web Vitals reporting
Chromium support, including attaching to a running browser via CDP (chromium.connectOverCDP)
Predefined device emulation settings to simulate mobile browser behavior
Screenshots captured during test runs and browser interaction timelines
Protocol-level load testing (HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket) combined with browser-level tests in a single script
CLI with script templates (k6 new --template browser), scheduling/automation from web app, CLI, and CI pipelines, SLOs as pass/fail criteria
Experimental native tracing of test runs, scenarios, VUs, and iterations via OpenTelemetry (added in v2.4.0)

grafana-k6-operator.about: Grafana k6-operator is a Kubernetes operator for running distributed k6 load/performance tests in a cluster. It defines two CRDs: TestRun (a single k6 test execution with configurable parallelism, script, args, and environment) and PrivateLoadZone (a load zone of cluster nodes integrated with Grafana Cloud k6 for running cloud tests inside your own cluster). It supports installation via bundle (kubectl apply), Helm chart, or Makefile/kustomize, and integrates with Grafana Cloud k6 via Private Load Zones and cloud output.
features: TestRun CRD for declaratively running a single distributed k6 test with configurable parallelism, script (ConfigMap), args, and environment variables
PrivateLoadZone CRD for hosting k6 load zones inside your Kubernetes cluster, integrated with Grafana Cloud k6
Two-level authentication for PrivateLoadZone tests using short-lived test run tokens (K6_CLOUD_TOKEN)
Cloud output mode to send test results to Grafana Cloud k6 (--out cloud, parallelism ≤ 20)
Installation via bundle.yaml, Helm chart (grafana/k6-operator), or Makefile/kustomize from tagged commits
Namespace-scoped watching via WATCH_NAMESPACE / WATCH_NAMESPACES environment variables
Synchronized distributed test execution across multiple k6 runner pods for accurate results at scale
Semantic versioning with a regular ~8-week minor/major release schedule since v1.0.0
grafana-k6-operator.pricing: Open source / free (OSS Kubernetes operator); PrivateLoadZone usage requires a Grafana Cloud k6 account with separate billing for the managed service.

guidellm.about: GuideLLM is an open-source platform from the vLLM project for evaluating how LLMs perform under real-world workloads and configurations. It simulates end-to-end interactions with OpenAI-compatible and vLLM-native servers, generates realistic workload patterns reflecting production usage, and produces detailed reports on latency, throughput, and token-level statistics to help teams tune deployments and plan capacity. It supports real and synthetic datasets (text, image, audio, video), multimodal inputs, and flexible execution profiles.
features: Complete latency and token-level statistics for SLO-driven evaluation (full distributions for TTFT, ITL, end-to-end behavior)
Realistic, configurable traffic patterns across synchronous, concurrent, and rate-based modes with reproducible sweeps
Support for real and synthetic multimodal datasets (text, image, audio, video)
Standardized, exportable reports (JSON/CSV/HTML, plot images) for dashboards, analysis, and regression tracking
High-throughput, extensible benchmarking with multiprocessing, threading, async execution, and flexible CLI/API
SLO-based goodput measurement and goodput profile that searches for maximum concurrency meeting a target SLO attainment
Trace replay of Mooncake, WEKA, and OTEL datasets including subagent branches and tool calling
Knee detection profile for finding maximum output token throughput
guidellm.pricing: Free; open source under Apache License 2.0
guidellm.authorOrCompany: vLLM project (vllm-project); PyPI package author listed as Red Hat

h2load.about: h2load is a command-line benchmarking/load-testing tool for HTTP/2 (and HTTP/1.1, plus experimental HTTP/3 when built with HTTP/3 enabled), shipped as part of the nghttp2 project. It supports SSL/TLS and cleartext connections, configurable concurrent clients, threads, and concurrent streams, and reports request rates, latency distributions, status codes, and connection statistics.
features: HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 benchmarking with SSL/TLS and cleartext support
Experimental HTTP/3 support via --h3 / --alpn-list=h3 (when built with HTTP/3 enabled)
Configurable number of requests (-n), concurrent clients (-c), threads (-t), and max concurrent streams (-m)
Timing-based load testing with --duration and --warm-up-time, plus fixed connection rate via -r/--rate
Flow control window tuning via -w (stream) and -W (connection) window-bits
Multiple URIs from command line or input file (-i), header override (-H), POST data (-d)
TLS options: cipher lists for TLSv1.2/1.3, SNI override, TLS session resumption (--tls-session-file), ktls
Performance statistics with histogram plotting (--histogram) and metrics including median, p95, p99, and QUIC-specific metrics

hammerdb.about: HammerDB is the industry-standard open-source database benchmarking tool, hosted by the TPC-Council. It runs TPROC-C (OLTP, derived from TPC-C) and TPROC-H (analytical, derived from TPC-H) workloads across Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, IBM Db2, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and VillageSQL, via GUI, CLI, web service and automation interfaces, with official Docker images for x86-64 and ARM64 Linux.
features: Multi-database benchmark engine: TPROC-C and TPROC-H workloads for Oracle, SQL Server, Db2, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and VillageSQL
GUI, CLI (Tcl/Python scripting), web service and automation interfaces
CI and pipeline automation that clones, builds, installs and benchmarks database branches/tags/commits (providers for MariaDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, VillageSQL)
Browser-based job views, benchmark reports, metrics, charts and repeatable automation workflows
Shareable result artifacts for saving, reviewing and publishing benchmark evidence through the TPC community results workflow
Official Docker images and reproducible workloads for container/cloud testing (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64)
Native Linux ARM64 (aarch64) builds and packages for Windows, RHEL 9 and Ubuntu 24.04
System discovery, CPU and I/O metrics (IOPS, MB/s), Active Session History analysis for Oracle, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB

Robot Framework tests written in plain English
REST and GraphQL API testing through authenticated browser sessions
Android/iOS real-device mobile testing via appium-device-farm

Email flow testing with disposable inboxes (verification codes, magic links, password resets)

SSL/TLS, DNS, WHOIS, security headers, SPF/DKIM/DMARC and email/IP/IBAN/VAT/phone validation checks

hey.about: hey is a tiny command-line HTTP load generator written in Go, an ApacheBench (ab) replacement. It sends a configurable number of requests to a web application at a given concurrency level and prints statistics (summary, latency histogram, percentiles, status code and error distributions). Rate limiting per worker in QPS (-q)
Duration-based runs (-z, e.g. 30s)
CSV output of response metrics (-o csv)
HTTP methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS (-m)
Custom HTTP headers (-H), request body from string or file (-d/-D), content-type (-T)
HTTP/2 support (-h2)
Basic authentication (-a) and HTTP proxy support (-x)

htstress.about: htstress is a fast HTTP benchmarking tool for Linux, written in C by Roman Arutyunyan (arut). It is similar to Apache Benchmark (ab) but adds multithreading support, which is essential for benchmarking high-load services (>5K rps). Configurable total number of requests (-n) and concurrency (-c); endless benchmark mode when -n is omitted
Reports good/bad request counts (1xx/2xx/3xx vs 4xx/5xx), elapsed seconds, and requests/sec
Linux CLI tool written in C with no external library dependencies
ab-like command-line arguments for easy migration from ApacheBench

httperf.about: httperf is a C-based command-line tool for measuring web server performance. It provides a flexible facility for generating various HTTP workloads and measuring server performance, supporting HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, and SSL/TLS protocols. It is designed for building both micro- and macro-level benchmarks, with robustness (including ability to generate and sustain server overload) and extensibility to new workload generators and performance measurements. It was originally developed at HP Labs (HP Research Labs) by David Mosberger and Tai Jin.
features: HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 protocol support
SSL/TLS support (via OpenSSL, with --ssl, --ssl-ciphers, --ssl-no-reuse options)
Configurable workload generation: request count (--num-conns), request rate (--rate), timeout (--timeout)
Flexible interarrival time specification via --period option (fixed, uniform, exponentially distributed)
Session-based workload generators with cookie support (--session-cookie, --wsesslog log-file based sessions)
Custom HTTP headers (--add-header) and HTTP method selection (--method)
Performance statistics: connection, request, reply, CPU time, network bandwidth, and error summaries
Retry-on-failure option (--retry-on-failure)

hyperfine.about: hyperfine is a command-line benchmarking tool that repeatedly executes programs and shell commands, statistically analyzes the measurements across multiple runs, and compares multiple command variants. It supports various performance metrics and hardware counters (wall-clock time, peak memory, CPU cycles, instructions, cache misses, branch misses), warmup runs, cache-clearing commands, statistical outlier detection, parameterized benchmarks, and export to CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc, and org-mode. Constant feedback about benchmark progress and current estimates
Warmup runs before the actual benchmark
Cache-clearing commands before each benchmark run (--prepare/--cleanup)
Statistical outlier detection to detect interference from other programs and caching effects
Export results to CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc, and org-mode (JSON schema v2 with metadata, per-run measurements, and statistical summaries)

iamspeed.about: I am speed (iamspeed.dev) is an open-source, browser-based, fast.com-style benchmarking tool for LLM APIs. perfgenie.about: perfGenie is a Salesforce open-source, continuous low-overhead contextual profiling solution that parses and visualizes Java Flight Recorder (JFR) profiles and Jstack thread dumps. JFR profiles can be created with JMC, Java Flight Recorder, Async-profiler, or jcmd. It supports viewing profiles as context trees, samples explorer, flame graphs, thread state, river, and 3D hotspot surface views, comparing two profiles via context tree or flame graph diff, filtering by custom event context/tid/thread name, request timeline views, and aggregating profiles over longer periods. It can be deployed as a continuous profiler using Cantor as a data layer (H2, MySQL, or S3 storage) with a cron job that monitors a directory for JFR/Jstack files, plus an agent mode.

Statistics on timing, data transferred, status codes, and more
Export raw data as TSV and/or JSON for analysis and graphs
HTTP/2 support

pgbench.about: pgbench is a simple benchmarking program included with PostgreSQL for running benchmark tests on PostgreSQL databases. It repeatedly runs the same sequence of SQL commands, possibly in multiple concurrent database sessions, and calculates the average transaction rate (transactions per second). By default it tests a TPC-B-like scenario with five SELECT, UPDATE, and INSERT commands per transaction, and supports custom transaction script files.
features: TPC-B-like default benchmark scenario with custom SQL transaction script support
Concurrent client simulation with configurable number of clients and parallel jobs
Built-in scripts (tpcb-like, simple-update, select-only) with weighted script selection
Per-statement latency, failure, and serialization/deadlock retry statistics (-r option)
Extended/prepared query protocol modes for faster query submission
Connection overhead measurement (-C) and new-connection-per-transaction testing
Initialization of standard benchmark schema (-i) with configurable scale factor
Cross-platform: runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows with only libpq dependency

plow.about: Plow is a high-performance HTTP(S) benchmarking/load-testing CLI tool written in Go by six-ddc. It uses the fasthttp library for fast request handling, runs a configurable number of concurrent connections against a target URL, and displays real-time summary statistics, latency histograms, and percentiles in both a terminal and a local web UI. It supports fixed duration or request-count runs, rate limiting, ramp-up, custom methods/headers/bodies, TLS client certificates, SOCKS5/HTTP proxies, Unix domain sockets, request-phase latency tracing, and a benchmark history feature for recording, browsing, and comparing runs.
features: Concurrent HTTP/HTTPS load generation with configurable connections (-c)
Rate limiting via token bucket (--rate) and ramp-up option (--ramp-up)
Run for fixed duration (-d) or fixed number of requests (-n)
Real-time web UI (default port 18888) and terminal display with live charts
Stream-based real-time histograms and quantiles (P50–P99.99) with low memory/CPU overhead
Custom HTTP methods, headers, host, content-type, and request bodies (including @file streaming)
TLS client certificates, insecure mode, and per-phase timeouts
SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy support, Unix domain socket connections

pureload.about: PureLoad is a commercial, self-hosted load and performance testing solution for applications and networks by Emblasoft (which acquired PureLoad in 2020). It emulates client applications/UEs at the protocol level (full-stack) to test IP-based applications in mobile networks, CDNs, and telecom services (e.g., RCS/RBM, IMS, 5G), scaling from single use cases to high traffic volumes, with GUI-based scenario building, automation, and DevOps/CI integration.
features: Full-stack protocol-level client simulation (HTTP, HTTPS, SIP, MSRP, Diameter, and other IP protocols) for applications and mobile networks
Scale from single use cases to high traffic volumes, simulating individual UEs/subscribers with unique IP addresses
Realistic payload validation and functional + performance testing in one tool
GUI-based test case and scenario building without programming
Automation and DevOps/CI/CD integration (PureLoad Runner server with Java API and command-line interface in Enterprise edition)
HTTP-based monitoring (complementing SSH and SNMP monitoring)
IPv6 support for internal communication
In-depth analysis/reporting: response times, traffic volumes, alerts, built-in KPI measurements from test-case to protocol level

pylot.about: Pylot (Python Load Tester) is a free, open-source web performance/load testing tool by Corey Goldberg. It runs HTTP/HTTPS load tests for capacity planning, benchmarking, analysis, and system tuning: it generates concurrent HTTP requests, verifies server responses (e.g., with regular expressions), and produces results reports with metrics and graphs. Test cases are defined in XML files and executed/monitored from a GUI (wxPython) or shell/console. The project is hosted on the archived Google Code project (code.google.com/archive/p/pylt) and is considered discontinued.

Response verification with regular expressions

Organizations, teams, and RBAC; SSO (SAML/OIDC) on paid plans
Web UI, CLI, official GitHub Action, API, and AI coding agent support (CLI skill)

visual-studio-load-test.about: Visual Studio Load Test is Microsoft's web performance and load testing capability built into Visual Studio (Enterprise), including web performance tests (.webtest), load test scenarios, and the Azure DevOps cloud-based load testing service. Visual Studio 2019 (version 16.x) was the last version with load test features; the cloud-based load testing service was shut down March 31, 2020 and officially retired April 29, 2021. Microsoft recommends Azure Load Testing (now Azure App Testing) or Apache JMeter as alternatives. Minimal support to run existing tests remains in Visual Studio 2022, but new-test templates were removed.
features: Web performance tests (.webtest) with HTTP request recording via Internet Explorer-based web recorder
Load test scenarios with load patterns (constant, step, ramp), test mix, network mix, and browser mix
Virtual user simulation with think time profiles and iteration-based or duration-based runs
Test Controller/Test Agent architecture for on-premises distributed load generation with weighted agent scaling
Cloud-based load testing via Azure DevOps with auto-provisioned or self-provisioned agents (retired March 31, 2020)
Performance counter data collection, threshold violations, and error reporting in load test results
Load test execution in Azure Pipelines via cloud-based load test, JMeter, and web performance test tasks (removed after EOL)
Export of test results to reports; results include performance counter data, threshold violations, and error information
visual-studio-load-test.pricing: Retired product with no current license or hosted service. Historically, load testing was included with Visual Studio Enterprise subscriptions (any number of virtual users, including production load tests), and the cloud-based service offered 15,000 free virtual user minutes per month with Azure DevOps; earlier licensing used a virtual-user-pack model (~$5,000 per load agent CPU era pricing).

wapt-pro.about: WAPT Pro is a scalable load/performance testing tool by SoftLogica for testing web applications, REST APIs, mobile applications and server components under load. It uses a workplace component plus distributed load agents/engines (locally or in cloud) to emulate up to 1M concurrent virtual users, with server and database monitoring, scripting, custom pass/fail criteria, and DevOps/Jenkins integration.

Cloud-ready: workplace and agents can run in virtual/cloud systems, remote agent management
Record user sessions with desktop or mobile browsers; AJAX/RIA support
Authentication schemes (Basic/Digest/NTLM/Kerberos, token-based) and client certificates; HTTPS/SSL/TLS support
Direct server performance monitoring via SNMP and WMI; database performance monitoring (ODBC; predefined counters for Apache, IIS, MS SQL, MySQL, Oracle)
Embedded JavaScript scripting for in-session data processing
Custom pass/fail criteria and custom test results analysis functions; export raw timing data to CSV
Real-time charts and customizable test report with 20+ tables; integrated log viewer with side-by-side comparison

webload.about: WebLOAD is RadView Software's enterprise-grade load/performance testing tool (since 1993) for web, mobile, and API applications. It lets users record or code test scripts (JavaScript/Java), simulate large numbers of concurrent virtual users from cloud or on-premise load generators, capture server-side metrics, and analyze results via a real-time browser-based dashboard, with CI/CD and APM integrations.

Automatic correlation engine for dynamic values (session IDs, tokens)
Load generation from cloud (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), on-premise, or hybrid; scales from 50 to 100,000+ concurrent virtual users
Protocol support: HTTP/S, WebSocket, REST APIs, plus enterprise protocols (SAP, Oracle Forms, Salesforce, MQ, JMS) in Enterprise edition
Real-time analytics dashboard with live run comparisons and reports
Server-side monitoring (Windows, Linux, web/app/database servers) during test runs
CI/CD integration: Jenkins, Atlassian Bamboo, Git, Selenium, Appium
APM integrations: Dynatrace, AppDynamics, New Relic, Nagios

weighttp.about: weighttp (pronounced 'weighty') is a lightweight, small C-based benchmarking/load-testing tool for webservers in the lighttpd project. It is designed to be very fast and easy to use, supporting a subset of the HTTP 1.x protocol, with multithreading for multi-core CPUs and event-driven I/O for concurrent requests within a single thread. It uses command-line arguments similar to Apache Bench (ab).
features: Multithreading for concurrent load generation across CPU cores
Event-driven I/O for concurrent requests within a single thread
HTTP keep-alive connections (-k)
Request pipelining (-K)
IPv6 support (-6)
HTTP HEAD and custom HTTP methods (-i, -m)
Custom request headers, cookies, Basic auth, proxy auth (-H, -C, -A, -P)
Proxy support including unix domain sockets (-X)

wrk.about: wrk is a modern, open-source HTTP benchmarking tool written in C with LuaJIT scripting, created by Will Glozer (wg) and maintained as a community project on GitHub. It is a multithreaded, event-driven (epoll/kqueue) CLI tool that generates significant load from a single multi-core machine, measuring throughput (requests/sec) and latency for HTTP/HTTPS endpoints.

Scalable event notification via epoll and kqueue
LuaJIT scripting for custom HTTP request generation, response processing, and custom reporting
Detailed latency statistics (--latency) with coordinated-omission correction
Custom HTTP headers, timeouts, and TLS SNI support
Single-binary CLI, self-hosted; supports macOS and Linux
Open source under Apache 2.0 (modified) license

wrk2.about: wrk2 is a constant-throughput, correct latency-recording variant of the HTTP benchmarking tool wrk, created by Gil Tene. It generates load at a fixed requests-per-second rate (via --rate/-R) and uses HdrHistograms for lossless latency recording, avoiding coordinated omission and enabling accurate high-percentile (up to 99.9999%) latency reporting. It is a free, open-source (Apache License 2.0) community project maintained by Gil Tene.
features: Constant throughput load generation via --rate/-R (default 1000 req/s)
Accurate latency recording to high 9s (e.g., 99.9999%ile) using HdrHistograms
Coordinated omission avoidance (latency measured from planned send time)
Multithreaded design with epoll/kqueue event notification
Lua/LuaJIT scripting API for request generation, response processing, and custom reporting (wrk-compatible stats objects)
Detailed latency percentile output (--latency flag) importable to spreadsheets/gnuplot
HTTP/HTTPS benchmarking with TLS/SSL support
Extended 10-second calibration period
wrk2.pricing: Free; open source under Apache License 2.0

xlt.about: XLT (Xceptance LoadTest) is an open-source load and performance testing tool developed and maintained by Xceptance, released under the Apache License 2.0. It is a Java-based (Java 21+), platform-independent tool for scalable, developer-centric performance testing: tests are written in pure Java as JUnit tests, can be run/debugged in any IDE, and scaled from a single laptop to thousands of concurrent users across many machines (on-premises or cloud, e.g., AWS/GCP). It provides detailed HTML reports (load test, comparison, and trend reports), a Result Browser with DOM snapshots and HAR data, flexible load profiles (user and arrival-rate models addressing coordinated omission), and open data formats.
features: Tests written in pure Java as JUnit, fully debuggable in any IDE
Flexible load profiles with user and arrival-rate models (addresses coordinated omission)
Extensive reporting: load test reports with runtime totals, averages, percentiles, SLAs, errors; comparison reports; trend reports with color-coded charts
Dynamic zoomable overview charts with tooltips in load test reports (9.2.x)
Result Browser with full DOM snapshots, network HARs, response bodies, and query strings in request names
Scalable distributed execution: master controller + agents across any number of machines/datacenters, automatic load distribution, offline coordination without data loss
Real browser support via Selenium WebDriver/HtmlUnit 4.x for complex setups
Platform independence: unzip-and-run, no OS dependencies; deploy to any cloud supporting Java 21+ (free AWS EC2 AMIs, XLT-Packer)
xlt.pricing: Free — 100% open source under the Apache License 2.0 with no license cost and no vendor lock-in (Xceptance offers paid services such as support, training, and hosted XTC SaaS separately).

Load profiles and scheduling (RPS schedules, dynamic thread limit, instances schedule)

ycsb.about: YCSB (Yahoo! Cloud Serving Benchmark) is an open-source Java benchmarking framework developed by Yahoo! Research that loads synthetic records into a datastore and runs configurable mixes of reads, updates, inserts, and scans to measure throughput and latency. It includes six core workloads (A–F) and supports 40+ NoSQL databases plus JDBC-enabled SQL/NewSQL databases through pluggable bindings.
features: Six core workloads (A: read/update mix, B: read mostly, C: read only, D: read latest, E: short ranges/scans, F: read-modify-write) with configurable read/write/scan/insert proportions
Supports 40+ NoSQL databases (Cassandra, MongoDB, Redis, HBase, DynamoDB, Azure Cosmos DB, etc.) and JDBC-enabled SQL/NewSQL databases via pluggable bindings
Zipfian, latest, and uniform request distributions for realistic access patterns
Latency and throughput measurement with HdrHistogram support, configurable percentiles (default 95th/99th), and histogram file output for merging across clients
Coordinated omission correction with intended-start-time measurement when target load is specified
Data loading phase plus transaction execution phase with client-side throttling to target throughput
Extensible workload framework: create custom workloads via new parameter files or Java classes extending site.ycsb.Workload
Multi-threaded client with configurable thread counts, field name prefixes, and client-side buffering
